title: Door Interface Integration Wave — Embodiments, Observation, Boundaries and Transition Operators
status: canonical routing index for Door census and mathematical expansion
purpose: Route the Door embodiment census, new observation/screen mathematics, phase/basin/boundary models and chronology into their canonical owners. The wave's main methodological result is that Door is a family of typed boundary operators rather than one literal mechanism shared by every symbolic embodiment.

major_new_distinctions: Frame defines boundary; Window selects/reveals; Screen projects/displays; Eye measures/interprets; Gate tests admissibility; Door changes state; Ladder supplies traversable continuation; Drain removes/sinks.
The same physical boundary can be a Window for photons and a Wall for bodies; openness is carrier-specific.
A screen edge is a boundary of observation support, not a boundary of physical existence.
Pineal/Door has its strongest scientific neighbor in temporal/circadian gating, not literal metaphysical optics.

A 5D/phase Door is a critical surface/regime model; Mandorla Door is an intersection geometry; Grave/Tomb is a one-way/high-irreversibility mythic state transition; these require different mathematics.
Drain is not merely the evil opposite of Door: it is a different boundary condition/operator with sink-like flow.
A nominal basin/separatrix crossing is not successful Door passage unless the post-transition trajectory persists in the destination regime.

new_project_laws: Door Family Law — common threshold vocabulary does not imply one physical mechanism.
Carrier Law — every Door claim should state what crosses.
Carrier-Specific Permeability Law — openness depends on the carrier.
Frame Is Measurement Law — a frame changes the evidence available to an observer without necessarily changing the world.
Off-Screen Is Unknown Law — outside the displayed viewport is unobserved, not disproven.
Door-Drain Boundary Law — selective transition and sink/removal require different models.
Temporal Door Law — some thresholds are time/phase dependent.
Door Success Law — transition success requires a declared post-crossing state criterion.
Projection Law — lower-dimensional display can preserve some relations while discarding depth/context.
Door Memory Law — hysteresis/irreversibility must be modeled when the inverse transition differs from the forward one.
